label: Digital Identity & eKYC for Inclusion
description: Design and assess digital-identity and eKYC RegTech for financial inclusion: national digital ID, tiered/risk-based KYC for the unbanked, GSMA mobile identity, and the privacy-vs-exclusion-vs-AML/CFT balance.

claudeKnowledge.description: FATF Recommendations 10 & 1 + FATF Guidance on Digital ID (2020) and Financial Inclusion (2017/2025 update); GSMA Mobile Money and Mobile Identity / Digital Identity programmes; World Bank ID4D and the Principles on Identification for Sustainable Development; ISO/IEC 29115 (LoA) and ISO/IEC 18013-5 (mobile driving licence / mDL); NIST SP 800-63-3 (IAL/AAL/FAL); eIDAS 2.0 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1183) and the EU Digital Identity Wallet; AMLR (EU) 2024/1624 remote-identification and eIDAS-means provisions; GDPR (EU) 2016/679 (Art. 9 biometrics, Art. 22 automated decisions, Art. 35 DPIA); national digital-ID schemes (Aadhaar/India Stack, BankID, MOSIP, national eID).

guidedInputs.label: Known Issues, Constraints or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe the specific design questions, known gaps, population characteristics, prior findings, or trade-offs you want addressed.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. We onboard agents and rural customers with low-coverage national ID; biometric fingerprint capture fails for manual labourers (high false-reject rate); regulator requires full KYC even for low-value wallets; concerns about SIM-swap and address-of-record reliability...

exampleInput: We are a mobile-money provider in a Sub-Saharan market launching a low-value wallet for first-time, mostly rural and undocumented customers. National foundational-ID coverage is roughly 60% and skewed against women and informal workers. The central bank's AML/CFT rules currently demand the same full KYC for a $5 wallet as for a full bank account, which is killing activation. We want to design a tiered, risk-based KYC ladder: a basic mobile-identity tier (SIM registration + self-asserted data + transaction/balance limits) that steps up to full eKYC against the national digital ID and a fingerprint/selfie check as customers transact more. Assess this against FATF Recommendations 1 and 10 and the FATF Digital ID guidance, map the identity assurance levels we actually need at each tier, and tell us where the design creates exclusion risk (biometric false-rejects, women without ID) and privacy risk (over-collection of SIM and biometric data), and how to argue the proportionality case to the regulator.

exampleValues.known_concerns: National ID coverage ~60%, skewed against women and informal workers. Regulator demands identical full KYC for a $5 wallet and a full bank account. Fingerprint capture has a high false-reject rate for manual labourers. Concerns about over-collection of SIM and biometric data and SIM-swap fraud on the address-of-record.
